standard.title: Technical Requirements for No Objection for Practicing Health and Safety Activities

notes: THIS DOCUMENT IS NOT A PEOPLE-COMPETENCY DOCUMENT AND IT DOES NOT BELONG IN PHASE 5. That is the headline finding and it should be acted on before the module catalogue is built. The scoping document's Phase 5 table lists it as 'NOC to practise H&S activities' alongside the Lifeguard, OHS Practitioner and OHS PIC schemes, which reads naturally as a licence for an individual to practise. It is nothing of the kind. 'Health and safety activities' here is a category of BUSINESS ACTIVITY on a Dubai commercial licence — salons, barbershops, henna salons, hair fixing centres, oriental baths, massage and relaxation centres, spa clubs, fitness clubs, laundries and cloth pressing — and the No Objection permit is a PREMISES approval granted against a furniture layout drawing before the shop opens. All 12 pages were rendered and read. There is NOT ONE competency requirement in the document: no role, no qualification, no training, no certificate, no examination, no issuing body for any person, and no validity period for anybody. 'competencies' below is empty by evidence, not by omission. What it actually is: a fit-out and layout permit with real, measurable spatial requirements, plus a matrix of which services each licensed activity may offer. WHY module_kind = compliance nonetheless. The requirements are numeric and objectively checkable against a layout drawing or a tape measure — one metre between hairdressing chairs, half a metre to the wall, service rooms not less than 6 square metres, corridors not less than 1.2 metres, 20 cm between laundry machines, half a metre of waterproofing around basins. An inspector, or a reviewer of the submitted layout, can be right or wrong about each. But note the SHAPE of the compliance is unusual for this product: it is a one-off gate at fit-out, not a recurring obligation. The document lists exactly five trigger events (new company or branch, modification of the furniture layout, adding an activity to the licence, change of location, mobile activity) and sets NO renewal, NO expiry, NO periodic re-inspection and NO validity period for the permit itself. There is therefore almost nothing for an obligations engine to schedule. Sold as a module it is a pre-opening checklist, not a monitoring subscription — a different commercial shape from every other Phase 5 module and worth saying so plainly before it is priced like the others. RENDER-AND-READ WAS ESSENTIAL AND PROVED ITS VALUE HERE, per section 7.14. The 'Table of permitted services according to activity' on page 12 is a 5-row by 7-column matrix whose entire content is green ticks and red crosses. THE TEXT LAYER RETURNS THE ROW AND COLUMN HEADERS AND NOTHING ELSE — every single cell value is invisible to extraction. Read from the rendered page, the matrix is: Gents/Ladies SALON may do hairdressing and hair wash, manicure/pedicure, facial and waxing, and may NOT do jacuzzi/sauna/steam, oriental or Moroccan bath, or massage. Gents/Ladies BEAUTY CENTER may do manicure/pedicure, facial and waxing, and may NOT do hairdressing or hair wash, jacuzzi/sauna/steam, oriental bath or massage. Gents/Ladies ORIENTAL BATH may do ONLY the oriental or Moroccan bath. Gents/Ladies MASSAGE AND RELAXATION CENTER may do ONLY massage. Gents/Ladies SPA CLUB may do ONLY jacuzzi/sauna/steam. Those exclusions are the commercially sharp part of the document — a spa club offering massage, or a salon offering it, is operating outside its permitted services — and a text-only extraction would have shipped the module with the headers and no rules at all. This is the strongest confirmation yet of the section 7.14 standing practice. EDITION: version V 3.0 and issue date 4 May 2024 come from inside the document. The footer prints the date in LONG FORM ('Issue Date: 4th May 2024', superseded '12th Sept. 2021'), so there is no day/month ambiguity and confidence is high — this is not a rule-2 case. Note the source_url sits under an /uploads/2024/07/ path, two months after the stated issue date, and the portal record date is 2024-07-25: neither is the issue date, and taking either would have been wrong. Code DM-HSD-SP06-NOPHSA2 uses an SP prefix rather than GU and carries no guideline number; guideline_no is null. DELEGATIONS AND ONWARD REFERENCES that scope this module: the appendix cross-refers to GU13 (fitness centres), GU19 (spa and massage centres), GU75 (ideal salons), GU76 (laundry), GU77 (salons, barbershops and beauty) and GU107 (consumer products storage) for compliance during operation and monitoring after the activity starts. So SP06 governs the door and those six guidelines govern the ongoing operation — SP06 says so expressly ('The institution must abide by the guidelines related to compliance during operation and related to monitoring after starting the activity, which are mentioned in the appendix'). All six sit in the scoping document's Phase 6 establishment-checklist group. THAT IS THE REAL PRODUCT INSIGHT HERE: SP06 is the front door to a Phase 6 bundle, not a Phase 5 module, and it should be sequenced with them. Mobile activities are further delegated to 'Technical guideline (01) for service vehicles and mobile commercial activities', which the document itself flags as AVAILABLE IN ARABIC ONLY — noted as an Arabic dependency, though SP06 itself is English and was extracted in full.

limits.display: leaving a distance of one meter between one chair and another
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to chairs for hair cutting and hairdressing services in salons and beauty centres: Gents Haircutting & Hairdressing Salon, Women saloon, Children Hairdressing, Henna salon, Gents and Ladies Cosmetic & Personal Care Centres, and Gents, Ladies and general Hair Fixing Centres.
limits.source_quote: Chairs for hair cutting and hairdressing services must be suitable, taking into account leaving a distance of one meter between one chair and another, and at least half a meter between the last chair and the wall.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Note the chair-to-chair distance (1 m) is DOUBLE the chair-to-wall distance (0.5 m) for hairdressing, whereas for manicure and pedicure both are 0.5 m — the two services have different spacing rules and must not be checked with a single figure.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum distance between the last hairdressing chair and the wall
limits.display: at least half a meter between the last chair and the wall
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to hairdressing and haircutting chair layouts in salons and beauty centres.
limits.source_quote: Chairs for hair cutting and hairdressing services must be suitable, taking into account leaving a distance of one meter between one chair and another, and at least half a meter between the last chair and the wall.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum by the 'at least' glyph.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum distance between manicure and pedicure chairs, and to the wall
limits.display: a distance of half a meter between one chair and another, and at least half a meter between the last chair and the wall
limits.qualifier_rule: Chairs and tables for nail cutting services (manicure and pedicure) must be in suitable places and SEPARATED FROM OTHER SERVICES in the salon, with a hand wash basin and a foot wash basin provided while the service is given.
limits.source_quote: Chairs and tables for nail cutting service (manicure and pedicure) must be in suitable places and separated from other services in the salon, taking into account leaving a distance of half a meter between one chair and another, and at least half a meter between the last chair and the wall, and to provide a hand wash basin and foot wash basin while providing the service.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Both the chair-to-chair and chair-to-wall figures are 0.5 m here, unlike hairdressing.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum floor area of a facial and waxing service room
limits.display: shall not be less than 6 square meters
limits.qualifier_rule: Rooms designated for facial and waxing services must be equipped with a comfortable movable bed free of defects, cracks and rust, with surfaces that can be cleaned and sterilised, and must have a designated hand wash basin WITHIN the room separate from the rest of the shop. Walls must be FIXED — no curtains, accordion partitions or any temporary partitions between service rooms are allowed.
limits.source_quote: The rooms designated for providing facial and waxing services must be suitable and equipped with a comfortable, movable bed free of defects, cracks and rust, with surfaces that can be cleaned and sterilized, and to have a designated hand wash basin within the room separately from the rest of the shop, and shall not be less than 6 square meters, and provided with fixed walls (no curtains, accordion partitions, or any temporary partitions between service rooms are allowed).
limits.note: Inclusive minimum by the 'not less than' glyph. The fixed-walls rule is as enforceable as the area figure and is easier to miss on a layout drawing, where a partition may not be annotated as temporary.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum floor area of a service room in oriental baths, massage centres and health clubs
limits.display: The area of the service room should not be less than 6 square meters
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to Men and Ladies Oriental Baths, Gents and Ladies massage and relaxation centres, and Gents and Ladies Spa Clubs. Each service room must have a connected DRESSING ROOM through which entry to the service room is made; rooms must be separated with only ONE bed or basin per room; curtains, accordion separators and temporary separators between service rooms are not allowed.
limits.source_quote: The area of the service room should not be less than 6 square meters. A dressing room must be provided for each service room and be connected to it, so that entry to the service room is through the dressing room first. ... Service rooms should be separated and only one bed/basin should be placed in each room. It is not allowed to use curtains, accordion separators, or any temporary separators between service rooms.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Same 6 m2 figure as the salon facial/waxing room but a different rule set — the one-bed-per-room and dressing-room requirements apply here and not there, so the two must be kept as separate checks even though the area matches.

limits.display: corridors with suitable spaces, the width of which is not less than 1.2 meters
limits.qualifier_rule: THE ONLY REQUIREMENT COMMON TO ALL FOUR ACTIVITY GROUPS — it is repeated verbatim in section 6-1 (salons and beauty centres), 6-2 (oriental baths, massage centres and health clubs), 6-3 (fitness clubs) and 6-4 (laundry and ironing). Applies universally to premises in scope.
limits.source_quote: Providing corridors with suitable spaces, the width of which is not less than 1.2 meters. (stated identically at p8 for salons, p8 for oriental baths and massage centres, p8 for fitness clubs, and p9 for laundries)
limits.note: Inclusive minimum by the 'not less than' glyph. Being universal, this is the single most reusable check in the module and the first thing to test on any submitted layout.

limits.parameter_label: Minimum extent of waterproofing material surrounding a hand wash basin
limits.display: surrounded by waterproofing material for a distance of not less than half a meter
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies across salons (basin for washing hair plus a separate one for washing hands in the common area), oriental baths and massage centres (a separate hand wash basin in EACH room individually), fitness clubs, and laundries. A separate hand wash basin is required in every case.
limits.source_quote: Providing a basin for washing hair and a separate one for washing hands in the common area, surrounded by a waterproofing material for a distance of not less than half a meter. (p8, salons) Provide a separate hand wash basin surrounded by waterproofing material for a distance of not less than half a meter in each room separately. (p8, oriental baths and massage centres) Provide a separate hand wash basin surrounded by a waterproof material for a distance of not less than half a meter. (p8 fitness clubs, p9 laundries)
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. Note the scope differs by activity: in oriental baths and massage centres the basin is required in EACH ROOM SEPARATELY, whereas in salons it is a common-area requirement. Same number, different count.

limits.display: Provide a distance between each device of not less than 20 cm
limits.qualifier_rule: Applies to Laundry Services and Cloth Pressing Services premises.
limits.source_quote: Provide a distance between each device of not less than 20 cm.
limits.note: Inclusive minimum. NOTE THE UNIT CHANGE: this is the only spatial requirement in the document expressed in centimetres rather than metres. Storing it as 20 in a metre-denominated field would be a factor-of-five error, and storing 0.2 loses the source glyph. Recorded in cm as printed, per the section 7.12 rule on verifying unit mapping.

limits.parameter_label: Table of permitted services according to licensed activity
limits.display: Salon: hairdressing/hair wash YES, manicure/pedicure YES, facial YES, waxing YES, jacuzzi/sauna/steam NO, oriental or Moroccan bath NO, massage NO. Beauty centre: hairdressing/hair wash NO, manicure/pedicure YES, facial YES, waxing YES, jacuzzi/sauna/steam NO, oriental bath NO, massage NO. Oriental bath: oriental or Moroccan bath YES, all six others NO. Massage and relaxation centre: massage YES, all six others NO. Spa club: jacuzzi/sauna/steam YES, all six others NO.
limits.source_quote: Table of permitted services according to activity (most common): Activity/Service | Hairdressing/hair wash | Manicure/Pedicure | Facial | Waxing | Jacuzzi/Sauna/Steam | Oriental/Moroccan bath | Massage — rows: Gents/Ladies salon; Gents/Ladies beauty center; Gents/Ladies oriental bath; Gents/Ladies massage and relaxation center; Gents/Ladies spa club
limits.note: READ ENTIRELY FROM A RENDERED IMAGE OF PAGE 12. The cell values are green tick and red cross glyphs that the PDF text layer does not expose at all — extraction returns the headers and nothing else. This is the section 7.14 blank-page trap in its purest form, and had render-and-read not been the default this table would have shipped empty or, worse, been assumed permissive. min_val and max_val are null because the content is a categorical permission matrix, not a numeric bound; if this module is built it needs its own activity-to-service lookup rather than the numeric limit shape. TWO CAVEATS THAT MUST TRAVEL WITH IT: the table is headed 'most common', so it is expressly NOT exhaustive of activities, and the three narrow activities (oriental bath, massage centre, spa club) permit exactly one service each — which is stricter than most operators would assume and is the highest-value finding in the document.

obligations.cadence_note: NO CADENCE, AND THE ABSENCE IS THE POINT — the permit has no stated validity period, no expiry and no renewal cycle anywhere in the document. It is triggered purely by events. The five stated triggers are: a new company or new branch; modification of the furniture layout; adding an activity to the commercial licence; changing the location of the institution; and mobile activity. So this obligation can never be 'overdue' on a date; it can only become due when the business changes. That makes it a poor fit for a due-date engine and a good fit for a change-triggered prompt, and it is the reason this module has a different commercial shape from the rest of Phase 5. Service turnaround is stated as one working day and the service is FREE. The obligation_type 'permit_renewal' is the closest available term in the closed vocabulary; the duty is really initial permit APPLICATION rather than renewal, since no renewal exists. Noted per rule 4.
obligations.trigger_event: new company or new branch; modification of the furniture layout; adding an activity to the commercial licence; change of location of the institution; mobile activity
obligations.applies_to: Owners of establishments within scope in the Emirate of Dubai — gents, women's and children's hairdressing salons, henna salons, gents and ladies cosmetic and personal care centres, gents, ladies and general hair fixing centres, men's and ladies' oriental baths, gents and ladies massage and relaxation centres, gents and ladies spa clubs, men's and ladies' physical fitness clubs, laundry services and cloth pressing services. Hotel establishments are EXCLUDED provided the shops are licensed under the hotel establishment licence only; where the shop holds a separate licence this guideline applies to it.
obligations.source_quote: Those institutions must apply for the service in the following cases: New company / new branch. Modification of the furniture layout. Adding an activity to the commercial license. Change the location of the institution. Mobile activity. (p5) Hotel establishments are excluded from the scope of service, provided that the shops are licensed under the scope of the hotel establishment license only. In case the shop providing the services has a separate license, this guideline shall apply to it. (p5)

obligations.cadence_note: Event-driven submission with a strict and easily-failed format rule. The application is made through the Dubai Municipality website with the furniture layout attached, showing ALL provided services, the furniture distribution, dimensions in METRES and areas in SQUARE METRES. The uploaded file must consist of a SINGLE PAGE ONLY; where the shop has two floors, one page must contain both floor plans. Note the review is returned for amendment ONCE ONLY — 'If it is not fulfilled, the request is returned for one time only' — so a second deficient submission is not simply corrected, which raises the cost of getting the layout right first time and is the clearest place this product could add value on this module.
obligations.trigger_event: application for the No Objection permit
obligations.applies_to: Applicant establishments — furniture layout drawing submitted via the DM website; response (Approved / Rejected / To be Amended or Completed) checked through the company's DM account; permit and approved proposed furniture layout received electronically
obligations.source_quote: The furniture layout, showing all provided services and furniture distribution and the dimensions in meters and areas in square meters. Note: The file to be uploaded onto the system must consist of a single page only with the furniture layout. In the event that the shop consists of two floors, one page must include the two floor plans. (p6) In case of completion, the request is approved, and the permit is issued. If it is not fulfilled, the request is returned for one time only. (p5)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing layout and licensing conditions with no cadence, checked at permit review. The activities shown on the furniture layout must match the list of activities on the commercial licence, per the permitted-services table in the appendix. The layout must contain NO medical, treatment or specialised services outside the H&S Department's scope, and approvals for any such activities must come from the relevant authorities. Construction or architectural approvals must be obtained from the building licensing authorities. WHERE THE COMMERCIAL LICENCE COVERS BOTH MEN AND WOMEN, the men's and women's sections must be COMPLETELY separated with a separate external entrance for each and NO common areas at all — an absolute rule with no exception offered, and one that is checkable directly from the submitted layout.
obligations.trigger_event: review of the furniture layout against the commercial licence
obligations.applies_to: All establishments in scope — alignment of layout with licensed activities, exclusion of out-of-scope medical or specialised services, building authority approvals, and complete separation of men's and women's sections with separate external entrances where both are licensed
obligations.source_quote: The activities mentioned in the furniture layout must be in accordance with the list of activities in the commercial license, according to the table attached to the appendix to this guideline. The furniture layout must not contain any medical, treatment, or specialized services outside the scope of work of the Health and Safety Department in Dubai Municipality ... The institution must obtain construction or architectural approvals from the concerned building licensing authorities. In the event that the commercial license includes activities intended for men and women, then it is necessary to completely separate the section for men and the section for women, with a separate external entrance for each section, and no common areas are allowed. (p6)

obligations.cadence_note: Standing fit-out requirements specific to fitness clubs and laundries, no cadence. Fitness clubs: a changing room must be provided with lockers for clothes; suitable distances must be provided between sports equipment, with the number and size of equipment suitable to the shop area — NEITHER 'SUITABLE DISTANCE' NOR THE EQUIPMENT-TO-AREA RATIO IS QUANTIFIED anywhere, so unlike the rest of the document these two cannot be checked against a number; special shock-absorbing rubber floors are required for sports equipment areas, with other areas smooth and cleanable. Laundries: the sections inside the shop must be INDEPENDENT of each other and must comprise receiving and sorting, washing and drying, ironing, delivery of ready-made items, storage for clothes and bedspreads, and a chemicals and products storage room — six distinct sections, which is a countable check even though no areas are given for them.
obligations.applies_to: Men's and Ladies' Physical Fitness Clubs; and Laundry Services and Cloth Pressing Services
obligations.source_quote: A changing room must be provided with lockers to put clothes. Provide suitable distances between sports equipment. The numbers and sizes of sports equipment must be suitable according to the area of the shop. Special floors must be available for sports equipment made of shock-absorbing rubber materials, while other places must be smooth and cleanable. (p8-9) The sections inside the shop must be independent from each other and contain the following: Section of receiving and sorting clothes / bedspreads; Section of washing and drying clothes / bedspreads; Section of ironing clothes / bedspreads; Section of delivery of ready-made clothes / bedspreads; Storage for clothes / bedspreads; Chemicals and products storage room. (p9)

obligations.cadence_note: THE HANDOVER TO THE OPERATIONAL REGIME, and the reason this document should be sequenced with Phase 6 rather than Phase 5. SP06 covers the permit at fit-out and expressly delegates everything about running the business to six other guidelines listed in its appendix: GU13 fitness centres, GU19 spa and massage centres, GU75 ideal salons, GU76 laundry activities, GU77 salons, barbershops and beauty, and GU107 consumer products storage. All six are in the scoping document's Phase 6 establishment-checklist group. No cadence is given here because the cadences live in those six documents. Mobile activities are further delegated to Technical Guideline (01) for service vehicles and mobile commercial activities, which SP06 itself flags as AVAILABLE IN ARABIC ONLY — an Arabic dependency reached from an English document, and the only Arabic-blocked content encountered in this whole Phase 5 pass. Enforcement of the terms and conditions sits under Local Order 11 of 2003 on public health and community safety.
obligations.trigger_event: commencement of the activity after the permit is granted
obligations.applies_to: All permitted establishments — compliance during operation and monitoring after starting the activity, governed by the appendix guidelines rather than by SP06 itself
obligations.source_quote: The institution must abide by the guidelines related to compliance during operation and related to monitoring after starting the activity, which are mentioned in the appendix to this guideline. (p6) To fulfill the requirements related to mobile activities, reference is made to the Technical guideline (01) for service vehicles and mobile commercial activities (Available in Arabic Only), in addition to fulfilling the technical requirements listed in this guideline. (p6) The necessary measures will be taken against violators of the terms and conditions stated in accordance with the instructions and regulations of Local Order 11 of 2003 regarding public health and community safety. (p7)
